title: Refactor Dedicated pool Terraform modules for idempotent apply + standardized orchestration outputs
author: Nina Petrova
body: Context: as part of the Provision-to-ready automation sprint, fleet-provisioner needs stable Terraform semantics (idempotent apply + predictable outputs) to safely create/expand Dedicated pools across regions/SKUs with retries. Our current pool modules have a few sharp edges: resource names derived from random suffixes, outputs that vary by env, and module boundaries that make it hard to consume consistent identifiers in orchestration. This PR refactors the Dedicated pool module layout to (a) make repeated applies safe (no unintended recreation) and (b) emit a standardized output contract consumed by provisioning orchestration. Summary of changes: 1) Idempotent apply improvements: normalize naming across resources with a single pool_name + pool_id prefix; remove random_id/random_pet usage from core resource names; add explicit lifecycle blocks where we intentionally allow drift without recreation (e.g., launch template metadata); tighten depends_on where implicit ordering previously caused flappy diffs; unify tags (including required tags for control plane registration). 2) Module structure cleanup: introduce modules/dedicated_pool as the single entrypoint; split out modules/dedicated_pool/network, modules/dedicated_pool/iam, modules/dedicated_pool/cluster_bootstrap, modules/dedicated_pool/nodegroups; existing root-level dedicated-pool stacks updated to use new module; add moved blocks to preserve state where we renamed resources/modules. 3) Standardized outputs: add a stable set of outputs with consistent names/types across environments so fleet-provisioner can register pools and drive subsequent stages without parsing Terraform state: pool_id, pool_name, region, vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, security_group_ids, cluster_name, cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca_base64, node_instance_profile_arn, node_role_arn, launch_template_ids (by nodegroup), asg_names (by nodegroup), gpu_sku, image_version, and a ready_for_bootstrap boolean that indicates Terraform reached the point where k8s bootstrap can proceed. These are intentionally orchestration-friendly (no env-specific naming, no computed strings that change across applies). Compatibility/rollout notes: - This keeps the existing variables surface mostly intact; the few renames are backward-compatible via deprecated aliases (documented below). - State is preserved via moved blocks for the affected module/resource names. Please apply in staging first and verify the plan is empty on second apply. - No behavioral changes to networking defaults in this PR; those guardrails are in a follow-up (PR #914). Variable changes: - dedicated_pool.pool_name: now required; previously inferred from customer + env. - dedicated_pool.pool_id: optional; if not provided, derived from pool_name via a deterministic slug. - deprecated: customer_name -> pool_name (alias retained for now). Validation: - Ran terraform fmt + validate for all env stacks. - Ran terraform plan twice in staging to confirm idempotency (second plan is empty aside from expected computed timestamps). Checklist: [x] terraform fmt [x] terraform validate [x] plan is stable on re-apply (staging) [x] outputs documented + example consumption snippet for fleet-provisioner [x] moved blocks added where needed [x] no changes to provider versions in this PR
commits: modules(dedicated_pool): introduce new module entrypoint and split submodules
terraform: normalize naming + tags; remove random suffixes from core resources
outputs: add standardized orchestration outputs + docs
state: add moved blocks for module/resource renames; keep backward-compatible variable aliases
tests: add staging plan smoke script + CI check wiring
ci_summary: CI: pass. Checks: terraform-fmt (pass), terraform-validate (pass), terraform-plan-staging (pass), tflint (pass). Re-ran terraform-plan-staging once after fixing a missing output type annotation.
conversation: Vanessa Ortiz (review): Can you confirm the second apply is clean for both create + expand paths? We’ve had issues where nodegroups force replacement on launch template diffs.

Nina Petrova (author): Yup. I validated on staging in two scenarios: (1) no-op reapply after initial create and (2) add a second nodegroup + reapply twice. The only diff I saw before this PR was LT metadata timestamp churn; that’s now ignored via lifecycle on the specific field. Added notes in docs/dedicated-pool-module.md under “Idempotency gotchas.”
Victor Alvarez (review): For networking outputs, can we also expose the private route table IDs? Fleet-provisioner needs them for some readiness checks.

Nina Petrova (author): I’d prefer not to expand the contract unless we know it’s required. I added vpc_id + private_subnet_ids + security_group_ids which should be sufficient for the networking checks we’ve discussed (DNS/TLS reachability uses subnets/SGs). If route tables become necessary, we can add in a follow-up without breaking consumers.
Miles Thornton (review): moved blocks look good, but I’m worried about the deterministic pool_id derived from pool_name. What about renames?

Nina Petrova (author): Agree it’s risky to allow implicit renames. pool_name is effectively immutable after initial creation; for rename cases we should treat it as a new pool (new state). I added a note in the docs and made pool_id explicitly overridable so orchestration can pin it and avoid accidental churn. We can also enforce immutability in config validation on the control plane side (ENG-2745).
Keiko Yamamoto (review): Any changes to ASG health check grace periods/timeouts? Those have affected bootstrap timing.

Nina Petrova (author): No functional changes there. This PR is scoped to naming/idempotency + outputs. I did add explicit timeouts blocks where Terraform was previously using provider defaults, but values match what we already use in prod (documented in the module README).
Gabe Wilson (review): Output contract: can we add a single JSON output blob so the orchestrator can consume it without having to map many individual outputs?

Nina Petrova (author): I kept outputs as discrete fields for Terraform ergonomics, but added an additional output `orchestration_outputs_json` that jsonencodes the contract (stable keys). That should make consumption easy for fleet-provisioner while keeping normal TF usage sane.
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Please add one more example: how to consume outputs in the wrapper and persist to the provisioning run record.

Nina Petrova (author): Added a short snippet in docs/dedicated-pool-module.md with `terraform output -json orchestration_outputs_json` and the expected keys. Also linked it to ENG-2743 for implementation.
Miles Thornton (review): Approved after the doc updates. Please keep PR #914 focused on defaults/guardrails to reduce blast radius.
Vanessa Ortiz (review): Approved. Let’s land this behind the staging feature flag and validate with one internal pool.
release_notes: Infra only: Dedicated pool Terraform stacks now have stable, orchestration-friendly outputs and improved idempotency for repeated applies/retries. No customer-facing behavior change expected; rollout via staging first.
